overview: Rise 5.99's Fly is a single 2100-line class with more than thirty modes dispatched from a ModeSetting, making it one of the largest movement modules in the client. The mode list spans vanilla capability flight (Vanilla, Creative), velocity-based flight (Jetpack, Damage, Wait for Damage, Mush, Viper), anticheat-targeted exploits (Verus, Verus Lag, VerusBlack, Verus AirJump, Spartan, Aac3, Vulcan, Vulcan2, Matrix1.17, Redesky, Kauri, Taka, Vicnix, Exempted Value, ACR, ACR2), block-assisted flight (BlockFly, Block Drop, MineBox, Hycraft, Bow Longjump, Bow Fly), and packet-buffer modes (Hypixel, Hypixel Fast Lag, Hypixel Blink, Hypixel Infinite, Minemenclub, Minemenclub 2, MCCentral, Air Walk, Collide, Old NCP). The class implements onPreMotion for per-tick motion writes, onPacketSend and onPacketReceive for packet rewriting and cancellation, and a vanilla kick-bypass helper that streams position packets to a ground scan and back.

sections.p: The module's state is a large field block: tick counters, stage and boost ticks, the starting location triple, a ConcurrentLinkedQueue of buffered packets, a lastMotion vector, and per-mode flags like hypixelStart, fly, dmged and setback. onEnable snapshots the position, stores the starting location, resets counters, optionally fakes damage by sending a health-update byte, and runs mode-specific setup such as the C0B sprint injection for Verus or the teleport-down position packet for Hycraft. onDisable restores the fov, speedInAir, fly capability and timer speed, then flushes any buffered packets through sendPacketWithoutEvent. onUpdateAlwaysInGui hides settings that do not apply to the active mode, which is how the enormous setting surface stays usable.

onPacketSend is where several modes hide their traffic. Block Drop cancels every outgoing C03 and injects a C06 pos-look when a C02 use-entity goes out; Hycraft cancels all C03 packets; MineBox cancels C03 packets while on the Minebox server; Vicnix rate-limits outgoing movement; Hypixel Blink and Spartan buffer outgoing packets and flush them on a timer or tick pattern; Minemenclub buffers everything except chat after a jump; and the Hypixel mode rewrites the onGround flag of outgoing C03 packets to true once the fly state and stage are active. onPacketReceive handles S08 teleports per mode (Hypixel sets a setback flag, Hycraft cancels and re-sends the teleport target as a C06, Minemenclub cancels, Vulcan resets its tick counter, Verus disables the module on flag, Block Drop cancels and records the teleport), cancels S12 knockback for most modes, and converts the knockback into a jump for Bow Fly.

The Vanilla and MineBox modes pin motionY to the fly speed setting (or a random sub-unit value for kick bypass) and strafe at the same speed; the optional Vanilla Kick Bypass in Packet mode runs handleVanillaKickBypass, which scans down to the ground in 8-block steps sending a C04 per step, then climbs back the same way, so the server sees a continuous grounded path. The Verus mode injects a sprint action packet on enable and disables itself when a teleport arrives; Verus Lag drops the event y by 20 plus a random amount every 20 ticks and fakes ground near 1/64 block boundaries. The Vulcan mode pins posY to the starting location and runs a timed motionY and strafe sequence on fixed hypixelTicks. The Hypixel mode sets timer speed to 2, finds a slime block in the inventory, places it to push itself up, and then flies with a fake ground flag, pitch near 90 and an 0.42 jump.

files.label: Fly.java (module)
files.explanation:
The entire module is this one file. onPreMotion contains the giant mode switch: Vanilla and MineBox write motionY and strafe from the fly speed, Verus and Verus Lag use the y-drop and ground-fake pair, Vulcan runs its timed motionY sequence against the pinned starting Y, Hypixel places slime blocks and fakes ground, Matrix1.17 swaps to a block item and sends C08 placements on a tick pattern, Jetpack and Mush accelerate motion directly, and the block modes (BlockFly, Block Drop, Hycraft) combine motion writes with position packets. onPacketSend then filters the outgoing stream per mode: C03 cancellations for Block Drop, Hycraft, MineBox and Vicnix, packet buffering for Hypixel Blink, Spartan, Minemenclub and Hypixel Infinite, and the onGround rewrite for Hypixel.

onPacketReceive is where the module defends itself. The S08 branch is per-mode: setback tracking for Hypixel, cancellation plus C06 re-send for Hycraft, cancellation for Minemenclub, timer reset for Vulcan, auto-disable for Verus, and position recording for Block Drop. The S12 branch cancels every knockback for the player entity and, in Bow Fly mode, converts it into a 0.42 vertical motion, while Minemenclub also cancels S27 explosions. The receive handler is also what makes the Hypixel mode resilient: every teleport sets setback, and outgoing C03 packets only get the onGround rewrite when setback, fly and stage are all active.

handleVanillaKickBypass is the file's third notable piece. It scans from the current y down to a computed ground in 8-block steps, sending one C04 position packet per step, then climbs back with the same step pattern and a final C04 at the original y, all gated by a 1-second groundTimer. The Vanilla mode's kick-bypass stream is therefore a burst of position packets every second, which is exactly the traffic pattern that movement checks see as a teleport ladder.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement physics envelope)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly compares every move against a physics envelope rebuilt from the world. The horizontal allowance comes from a speed estimation based on sprint state and potion effects, and the vertical allowance from vDistRel, which inherits momentum from the previous move and only accepts named envelopes: a zero-y move on ground, a jump, a step-up and a riptide launch. Ground is derived from a block ray trace, not the packet flag, so the module's ground fakes do not relax anything. A violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 with a set-back to a stored location.

The fast horizontal modes hit the horizontal side immediately. Vanilla and MineBox strafe at the fly speed setting, which defaults to 1.0 and can go to 9.5, versus a sprint prediction near 0.31, so hDistanceAboveLimit is several blocks and the violation is in the hundreds on the first move. Verus Lag's y-drop of 20 plus a random amount presents a vertical delta of roughly 20 blocks against an allowed descent of a few tenths, an immediate yDistanceAboveLimit of about 19.7 and a violation over 1900. The Vulcan mode's 3.7 motionY spike is a legal single jump magnitude but the sustained flight around it, with posY pinned and motionY zeroed, produces the airborne zero-y hover the envelope does not name.

The kick-bypass ladder is the clearest case. Each C04 in the 8-block fall and climb pair is an 8-block vertical move with onGround true; NCP's ray trace says the claimed spot is air, so the ground flag is ignored and yDistanceAboveLimit lands near 7.7 per packet, with the whole ladder crossing the violation threshold on the first step. The block-assisted modes (BlockFly, Matrix1.17's C08 stream, Hycraft's C03 cancellation) fare no better, because SurvivalFly measures actual position deltas, and the module's own teleport or block-place tricks show up as unexplained position jumps.

countering.label: Flight (hover, ascension, glide)
countering.explanation:
Arc v2's Flight checks the vertical profile of every move. The hover check fires when both the last and current vertical speeds are exactly 0.0 and airTicks passes maxHover. Most Rise 5.99 modes hover by design: Vanilla pins motionY to 0 when no key is held, Vulcan zeroes motionY after its spike sequence, Jetpack resets ticks when the jump key is released, and the Hypixel mode sets motionY to 0 every tick while airborne, so the vertical speed is exactly 0.0 tick after tick and the hover flag fires once the air-time threshold is crossed.

The ascension branch compares the rising vertical speed against the jump cap. Vanilla's motionY of flySpeed (up to 9.5), Jetpack's ticks/30 acceleration, Vulcan's 3.7 spike and the 0.42 jumps in Hypixel all exceed the jump-derived cap on the first rising move, flagging ascending_too_fast. The descending branch requires the vertical change to match a gravity-derived polynomial; Verus Lag's 20-block drop and the immediate ground fakes make the glide delta enormous, tripping the glide or descend flags. Even the small timer-speed abuse in Redesky and Old NCP shows up as vertical profile changes the polynomial does not explain.

The check has a blind spot worth naming: horizontal-only modes that never change y (MCCentral's hover at a fixed y, Air Walk) avoid the ascension and descent branches entirely, and only the hover branch can touch them. That is why the module's own modes that fly with a constant y, such as Air Walk and Collide, are the ones that survive Arc the longest; everything with a vertical component gets flagged.

countering.label: Fly (predicted-velocity discrepancy)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's Fly runs a per-player vertical simulation. In air it predicts the next velocity as (previous estimated velocity - 0.08) * 0.98 and integrates it into an estimated position; the reported Y is compared against that estimate, and any discrepancy over the 0.0001 threshold is punished with a rubberband set-back. The hover modes fail the model immediately: Vanilla's zero motionY while airborne diverges from the predicted fall of about 0.0784 per tick within one or two ticks, and the module's motionY writes of several blocks per tick produce discrepancies of multiple blocks.

The trajectory modes fail differently. Verus Lag's 20-block drop is a position delta no gravity simulation produces, so the estimated position and the reported position separate by tens of blocks and the rubberband fires on the first drop. Vulcan's pinned posY with periodic 3.7 spikes creates a sawtooth profile that the integrator never matches. The Hypixel mode's timer speed of 2 doubles the tick rate, so even its small motion writes are reported at twice the rate the simulation expects. When the client reports onGround, the check also requires the reported Y to fall between the previous Y and the estimated position, so the ground fakes in Verus Lag, Vulcan2 and the Exempted Value modes, which claim ground while the position is mid-air, land outside that window.

The check tolerates at most 20 ticks without a position update, so the packet-buffer modes (Hypixel Blink, Spartan, Minemenclub) cannot hide by holding back movement packets. The modes that convert flight into block interaction, such as BlockFly and Matrix1.17 with their C08 placement streams, produce movement that the vertical model partly explains, but the horizontal acceleration from the placement is still outside the gravity-only prediction.
